historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2019-FY2026 revenue CAGR of 5.1% (pre-COVID base), tempered toward capacity growth of ~3% plus modest yield
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: shareholders' equity was 10 at FY2023 and negative at FY2022 after COVID losses and buy-backs, so any CAGR off those bases is meaningless. The 5-year revenue CAGR (33.9%) starts from the FY2021 COVID trough of 5,934 and is not a growth rate. EPS and owner-FCF 5-year CAGRs start from negative values and are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less share-based payments; no interest strip because the Group is in net debt): FY2019 1,171, FY2023 2,334, FY2024 699, FY2025 392, FY2026 -183. The series falls as net capex rises from 2,563 (FY2023) to 3,972 (FY2026) for fleet renewal; the 3-year CAGR ends on a negative value and is undefined. Share-based payments are 0.2-0.9% of revenue and do not drive the trend.

scenario_narratives.base: Fuel stays elevated through FY2027 and the 8-10% unit-revenue increase roughly pays for it, so the margin stands still for a year. From FY2028 fuel eases, the new narrowbody and A350 fleet lowers fuel burn and maintenance cost, Project Sunrise delivers part of its ~$400m EBIT target and Loyalty keeps growing at 5-7%. The domestic duopoly with Virgin stays rational at roughly equal shares. The EBITDA margin returns to 20%, the FY2025 level, and stays there. Fleet renewal keeps net capex above $4bn until FY2031, so free cash flow is negative in FY2027, about nil in FY2028 and only builds to ~$2.2bn (6% of revenue) once capex falls back toward depreciation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel normalises quickly while fares hold, as they did in FY2023. Project Sunrise earns the full ~$400m on Sydney-London and Sydney-New York with a premium-heavy cabin, the premium share of capacity rises from 19% to 28% as planned, and Loyalty grows EBIT near 10% a year on financial-services and business-rewards partners. Virgin prioritises margin over share. The EBITDA margin reaches 21.5% (EBIT ~11.7%, between FY2025's 11.1% and FY2023's 13.5%) and revenue grows 5-7% for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: A second fuel or geopolitical shock, or a consumer downturn, arrives while the fleet orders are committed. Corporate and government travel, already soft in late FY2026, weakens further; Virgin uses its relisted balance sheet to add domestic capacity and fares fall as fuel does. Sunrise is delayed or fills at lower yields, and a labour dispute or further legal penalty adds cost. The EBITDA margin dips to 16% and only recovers to 18%, an EBIT margin near 8% as in FY2017-FY2019, while capex can be deferred only slightly. With $7.1bn of lease-inclusive net debt, most of the enterprise value goes to lenders: this is a leverage outcome, not a solvency one, since liquidity and the Baa2 rating leave room to slow deliveries.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Qantas is valued as an operating company on unlevered owner free cash flow, with every lease counted as debt and fleet renewal charged in full through capex. The value sits almost entirely beyond FY2031: the next four years of cash flow are consumed by the largest fleet programme in the Group's history, so the valuation is a judgment about the margin and capex level after renewal, capitalised at 15x free cash flow (about 4.5x EBITDA, where the shares trade today). Leverage makes the per-share value very sensitive to that margin: two points of EBITDA margin separate the bear and base cases.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal EBITDA margin: each 1 point held across the forecast and the terminal year is worth roughly $2 per share because $7.1bn of net debt sits ahead of the equity
Post-renewal capex: the model assumes net capex falls from ~17% to 10.8% of revenue by FY2035; if replacement cost keeps capex near 13%, base value falls by roughly 40%
Fuel and geopolitics: FY2026 lost ~$420m net to one conflict and the 1H FY2027 fuel bill is guided at ~$3.75bn
Domestic competition: Virgin Australia is at share parity; the duopoly's pricing discipline is assumed, not guaranteed
Project Sunrise ramp-up: ~$400m EBIT target rests on a first-of-type aircraft entering service from CY2027
Loyalty is valued inside the group margin, not separately; a standalone multiple on its $625m EBIT would give a higher sum-of-parts than this model

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,513.2m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR note on issued capital, unchanged all year) plus 16m dilutive potential ordinary shares from the FY2026 EPS note. Held FLAT because share-based payments are expensed in the flows; the cash mechanism is on-market treasury-share purchases for the employee share trust ($87m FY2026, $133m FY2025).
inputs.net_debt_note: Interest-bearing liabilities 504 current + 8,107 non-current = 8,611; lease liabilities 401 + 1,340 = 1,741 (all leases, aircraft and property); cash 3,274. Qantas's own Financial Framework Net Debt is 6,161 (net on-balance-sheet debt 5,362 + capitalised aircraft leases 799) because it counts only aircraft leases; this model counts every AASB 16 lease liability, hence 7,078.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was 106 in FY2026 but the Group is in net debt (7,078), so there is no cash pile being double-counted; nothing stripped. The forward flows are unlevered (no interest received or paid) and gross cash is netted in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 26(E) share-based payments expense 104 (FY2025 56, FY2024 69, FY2023 188); statement of changes in equity agrees. No net-share-settlement tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes 0 throughout).
inputs.buyback_note: No on-market buy-back in FY2026: the $150m programme announced Feb 2026 was never started and was cancelled on 27 Aug 2026. FY2025 448, FY2024 852, FY2023 1,000. Dividends paid 700 in FY2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: 10-year ACGB ~4.4% risk-free, ~6% Australian ERP, airline equity beta ~1.2 gives cost of equity ~11.5%; pre-tax debt ~5.5% (Moody's Baa2), 3.9% after 30% tax; capital weights ~62% equity / 38% lease-inclusive net debt at market. That is ~8.6%, rounded up to 9.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: fuel, demand and competition risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: all 1,741 of AASB 16 lease liabilities sit in net debt; lease principal (319) and lease interest (88) are NOT deducted from the flows; EBITDA is post-AASB 16 and D&A includes right-of-use depreciation (337). Lease renewal is charged through the capex path: ~1.2% of revenue is added to guided net capex in every year to replace right-of-use assets as they run off (FY2026 lease principal repaid 319, new leases 539).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are 5 on the balance sheet with nil profit share in FY2026; ignored.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (AUD WACC, single lease treatment, risk charged once). Chosen because Qantas is an operating company whose value is its cash flow; it is not a bank, REIT or holdco. First valuation of this ticker. FY0 anchors: underlying EBITDA 4,596 on revenue 25,516 (18.0%); share-based payments (104) are already an operating expense inside that figure, so the engine's EBITDA margin path is stated BEFORE share-based payments (FY2026 18.4%) and the SBC path then charges it once. FY2026 absorbed ~420 net of hedging from Middle East fuel prices; ex that the margin was ~20%, in line with FY2025's 19.7%. FY2026 reported FCF is negative (-79) because net capex of 3,968 is at a fleet-renewal peak, not because the business is cash-burning: cash generated from operations was 4,736. Cash tax paid was 642 in FY2026 including a FY2025 true-up; COVID tax losses are used up, so the path runs at 29-30% on unlevered EBIT. Working capital: revenue received in advance (tickets sold ahead and unredeemed points) is 9,085 and grew 342 in FY2026; a 5% capture on revenue growth is used in the base case as a net figure after receivables and inventory. Equity bridge deducts the $300m FY2026 final dividend (declared Aug 2026, paid after the balance date, so the price is ex-dividend but June cash is not) and the $105m flight-credits class-action provision (settled, unpaid at balance date, pending Federal Court approval). NOT in the bridge: Jetstar Japan sale proceeds (~JPY8.2bn, well under A$100m, completion targeted by June 2027). Terminal value: Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% is 15.8x FCF, so the 15x cap binds in base and bull; 15x terminal FCF is ~4.5x year-10 EBITDA, against ~4.8x lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA today, so no multiple expansion is assumed. SBC is small (0.4% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027: 1H total unit revenue guided +8-10% on roughly flat group capacity (domestic -3%), second half unguided and assumed softer as fuel-driven fares ease. Then capacity growth of ~3% a year plus Project Sunrise from CY2027 and Loyalty growth, fading to 3%.
base.margin_rationale: Stated before share-based payments. FY2027 held just under FY2026 (18.4%) because the 1H fuel bill is guided at ~3.75bn against 5.7bn for all of FY2026, offset by the unit-revenue increase. Recovery to 20.0% by FY2031, the FY2025 level (19.7%) plus part of the Sunrise uplift; terminal EBIT margin ~10.2% against 11.1% in FY2025 and 9.2% in FY2026.
base.capex_rationale: FY2027 = guided net capex at the low end of 4.3-4.6bn (4.35bn) plus ~0.3bn lease renewal on revenue of ~27.0bn. Stays above 4bn through FY2031 while next-generation aircraft go to ~70% of capacity, then falls to 10.8% of revenue, about 1.14x D&A, which funds 3% growth and aircraft price inflation.
base.da_rationale: FY2026 2,278 = 8.9% of revenue, up from 8.4%; rises with the new fleet to ~9.6% and settles at 9.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: an airline with unhedgeable multi-year fuel and demand exposure, committed capex of $4bn+ a year and FY2026 already showing how one fuel shock takes two points off the margin; not higher because the balance sheet is investment grade and inside its own net-debt range. Base 50%: it is management's own framework (margin back to FY2025 levels, capex easing after the renewal peak). Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs fuel to normalise, fares to hold, Sunrise to deliver in full and Virgin to stay disciplined, four largely independent things.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
